news.headline: Christa Pike has 'profound' health turnaround after botched execution, lawyers say
news.story_lead: Watch: What we know about Christa Pike's "shock" recovery in hospital - Published 9 October 2026, 03:09 BST Christa Pike has made a "profound" turnaround after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, her lawyers say. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995. She survived two injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September and was taken to hospital in a critical condition.
news.full_article_text: Watch: What we know about Christa Pike's "shock" recovery in hospital - Published 9 October 2026, 03:09 BST Christa Pike has made a "profound" turnaround after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, her lawyers say. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995. She survived two injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September and was taken to hospital in a critical condition. Pike's lawyers described her recovery as "remarkable" and said in a statement on Thursday that she was able to walk with assistance and was eating. She had also regained some movement in her arms, which were badly injured during the attempted execution, they said. "Physicians are encouraged by her physical recovery," the statement said. The case is now in uncharted territory as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection. "Christa is dealing with the profound psychological trauma of having survived a failed execution, including the terror, pain and uncertainty of believing she was about to die," her legal team said. Pike's lawyers said they do not know the full emotional and psychological toll of the execution attempt or how long it will take her to recover. They added that while she was struggling to process what had happened, she "continues to express concern for others, particularly the family of her victim Colleen Slemmer". Slemmer's mother, who was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death, has branded the failed execution a "mess". Pike's boyfriend at the time of Slemmer's murder, Tadaryl Shipp, was spared the death penalty as he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison. Pike was 18 and Shipp was 17 when they beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people. - Could Christa Pike face execution again and by what method? Published 1 day ago A court has ordered officials to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution, which could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state. On Wednesday, Judge I'Ashea Myles ordered that "anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained", including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, such as packaging, inserts and labels. The judge also demanded documentation on Pike's psychological condition before, during and after the failed execution. She advised the state to take "special care" not to misplace or accidentally delete any information that may be pertinent to the case. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered a pause on all executions for the rest of the year and said he wants answers about what went wrong. Pike's lawyers have called on the governor to downgrade Pike's punishment to life in prison without parole. Proponents of capital punishment have suggested using a different method to put her to death. Could the US death penalty ever die out? news.headline: Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
news.story_lead: Dr Vincent Brown attended a previous court hearing in person - Published 9 October 2026, 12:42 BST A doctor accused of a number of offences relating to the 1994 Rwanda genocide is set to face trial in autumn next year. Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, is accused of "killing, directing or encouraging" the deaths of members of the Tutsi ethnic group in Rwanda. He is the first person in the UK to have been charged over the genocide.
news.full_article_text: Dr Vincent Brown attended a previous court hearing in person - Published 9 October 2026, 12:42 BST A doctor accused of a number of offences relating to the 1994 Rwanda genocide is set to face trial in autumn next year. Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, is accused of "killing, directing or encouraging" the deaths of members of the Tutsi ethnic group in Rwanda. He is the first person in the UK to have been charged over the genocide. Brown, of Islington, north London, is charged with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity. A judge has now set his provisional trial date to begin in October 2027. He denies wrongdoing and has not yet entered a plea. The defendant appeared via video link from Belmarsh prison on Friday for a pre-trial hearing at the Old Bailey during which Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb set a provisional eight to 12-week trial from October 4 2027. A plea and case management hearing has also been set for 15 January. He has indicated he will plead not guilty to the charges against him. An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and politically moderate Hutus were killed during the 1994 Rwanda genocide which lasted for 100 days . Brown is a medical doctor who qualified in Rwanda in the 1980s. He later became head of the country's Department of Family Health in Kigali and lived in a suburb there with his wife and young son. Between April 6 and 13 1994, he was allegedly a party to six murders and was later charged following a seven-year British investigation into the killings. The court heard on Friday that a Â£100,000 bail condition , imposed earlier in October, had not yet been met. Prosecutor Bill Emlyn Jones KC told the court the events in 1994 were "the most devastating wave of mass killing in modern history". Jones said: "One hundred thousand were murdered in Kigali especially in the first days and weeks of the genocide." Related topics

news.headline: Rajasthan orders weapons, vehicles for forest staff amid attacks linked to illegal sand mining
news.story_lead: Rajasthan orders weapons, vehicles for forest staff amid attacks linked to illegal sand mining Rajasthan chief secretary V Srinivas orders weapons and vehicles for forest staff in vulnerable Chambal sanctuary areas amid attacks linked to illegal sand mining. Rajasthan chief secretary V Srinivas has directed officials to ensure the timely provision of weapons and vehicles to forest personnel deployed in vulnerable areas of Rajasthan’s National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary and called for a joint action plan to curb illegal sand mining, amid a series of attacks on frontline personnel confronting mining operators. Chairing a state-level coordination and monitoring committee meeting convened on the directions of the Supreme Court, Srinivas stressed a zero-tolerance approach towards illegal mining, stronger field patrolling and inspections of vulnerable areas by senior officers.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan orders weapons, vehicles for forest staff amid attacks linked to illegal sand mining Rajasthan chief secretary V Srinivas orders weapons and vehicles for forest staff in vulnerable Chambal sanctuary areas amid attacks linked to illegal sand mining. Rajasthan chief secretary V Srinivas has directed officials to ensure the timely provision of weapons and vehicles to forest personnel deployed in vulnerable areas of Rajasthan’s National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary and called for a joint action plan to curb illegal sand mining, amid a series of attacks on frontline personnel confronting mining operators. Chairing a state-level coordination and monitoring committee meeting convened on the directions of the Supreme Court, Srinivas stressed a zero-tolerance approach towards illegal mining, stronger field patrolling and inspections of vulnerable areas by senior officers. He also directed departments to coordinate their efforts and submit compliance reports on time. The directions follow multiple attacks linked to alleged illegal mining, prompting renewed concerns over the safety of personnel deployed to prevent unlawful excavation and transportation of sand. Police constable Surendra Singh was injured after a speeding tractor-trolley allegedly involved in illegal sand mining ran over his leg in Sawai Madhopur’s Chauth Ka Barwara area on October 7. He was referred to Jaipur for treatment, while the elderly woman also sustained injuries. The driver fled the spot. The incident is the latest in a series of alleged attacks on police and forest personnel involved in action against illegal mining in eastern Rajasthan. On the night of September 21, forest ranger Pratap Singh Chundawat, posted in Rajasthan’s Pratapgarh district, was dragged by a dumper when he tried to flag down the vehicle, suspecting illegal mining. Following his death, the Supreme Court on September 23 directed the Rajasthan government to file a report as it examined the continuing menace of illegal sand mining in the Chambal sanctuary. In another incident on September 26, a forest team was allegedly attacked with stones and gunfire after seizing a tractor-trolley and a compressor machine during action against illegal mining near Kondapura village in Bharatpur district. Earlier, forest personnel were allegedly attacked in Tonk in August, while a forest outpost in the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve was attacked in March, with an arrested person freed and a seized tractor-trolley taken away. The Supreme Court has directed Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh to strengthen surveillance, establish checkposts, take action against organised mining networks and protect frontline forest personnel. It has also asked the states to consider preventive detention against alleged kingpins and habitual offenders involved in organised illegal sand mining. Against this backdrop, Srinivas emphasised the need to strengthen field-level security and improve coordination among departments to ensure effective enforcement. During his visit to Kota, the chief secretary also inspected the cyber police station, New Medical College Hospital and Kota Super Thermal Power Station, besides reviewing the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari campaign. At the cyber police station, he reviewed registered cases, investigations, arrests and the status of charge sheets. He said better coordination between banks and police, along with timely information-sharing, could help protect cyber fraud victims. He directed officials to raise the issue in District Level Bankers’ Committee meetings. At New Medical College Hospital, Srinivas called for complete digitisation of government hospitals while keeping patient care the priority. He stressed improving medical education, research and publications, as well as strengthening maternal and child healthcare services. He directed officials to ensure early identification and regular monitoring of high-risk pregnancies, adequate antenatal check-ups and blood supplies, adherence to treatment protocols and better referral transport facilities. He also inspected the neonatal intensive care unit and maternity ward and interacted with a patient admitted for delivery.

He said better coordination between banks and police, along with timely information-sharing, could help protect cyber fraud victims. news.story_lead: Student’s death triggers protests at Kota’s Rajasthan Technical University The protesting students accused the university administration of negligence and demanded chief warden’s removal A student’s death triggered protests at Rajasthan Technical University (RTU) in Kota, with police resorting to force to disperse agitating students after the demonstration escalated on Thursday. The first-year information technology student from Jaipur was found dead in his hostel room. Students alleged that he died of a snakebite on the campus.
news.full_article_text: Student’s death triggers protests at Kota’s Rajasthan Technical University The protesting students accused the university administration of negligence and demanded chief warden’s removal A student’s death triggered protests at Rajasthan Technical University (RTU) in Kota, with police resorting to force to disperse agitating students after the demonstration escalated on Thursday. The first-year information technology student from Jaipur was found dead in his hostel room. Students alleged that he died of a snakebite on the campus. The university administration said he may have suffered a cardiac arrest. The exact cause of death will be established after the postmortem report, officials said. The protesting students accused the university administration of negligence and demanded the removal of chief warden DK Yadav. They alleged that the campus dispensary closes at 2am and doctors are often unavailable, claiming that timely medical attention could have saved the student’s life. Students claimed that snakes had been spotted on the campus on several occasions. They staged a sit-in, insisting that their demands be addressed. Yadav said when Sharma was found unresponsive, the university team rushed to his room and arranged to take him to hospital in an autorickshaw. He added that doctors indicated that the student had died in his sleep between 4am and 6am. Yadav said the circumstances would become clear after the postmortem report. Police attempted to persuade the students to end their protest, but when they refused to disperse, force was used. Officials said the situation became difficult to control after some students allegedly began throwing stones. Additional police superintendent Subhash Chandra Mishra said the protesters demanded that the vice-chancellor come to the spot so they could present their demands. He added that several rounds of talks were held, following which the vice-chancellor agreed to some of the demands. Mishra said no agreement was reached on all demands, but the students eventually called off their protest. Police assured them that the circumstances surrounding the student’s death would be investigated impartially.

news.headline: BJP sweeps Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls with big wins for Hasirani Rath, Shankharavh Sarkar
news.story_lead: BJP sweeps Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls with big wins for Hasirani Rath, Shankharavh Sarkar BJP candidate Hasirani Rath, mother of slain Suvendu Adhikari aide Chandranath Rath, secured 1,64,427 votes in the Nandigram Assembly bypoll. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly bypolls in West Bengal, with candidates Hasirani Rath and Shankharavh Sarkar defeating their respective rivals by significant margins. In Nandigram, Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes, securing 1,64,427 votes, or 75.94 per cent of the total.
news.full_article_text: BJP sweeps Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls with big wins for Hasirani Rath, Shankharavh Sarkar BJP candidate Hasirani Rath, mother of slain Suvendu Adhikari aide Chandranath Rath, secured 1,64,427 votes in the Nandigram Assembly bypoll. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly bypolls in West Bengal, with candidates Hasirani Rath and Shankharavh Sarkar defeating their respective rivals by significant margins. In Nandigram, Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes, securing 1,64,427 votes, or 75.94 per cent of the total. Pradhan received 41,674 votes, accounting for 19.25 per cent of the votes polled. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, a close aide of West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari who was killed in May, days after the BJP won the state Assembly elections. In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won with 1,29,914 votes, defeating Golam Nabi Azad (Robin) of the Aam Janata Unnayan Party, who received 54,098 votes. Sarkar won by a margin of 75,816 votes. Why the bypolls were held The Rejinagar Assembly bypoll was held because Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief Humayun Kabir vacated the seat after winning both Rejinagar and Naoda in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. He chose to retain Naoda, necessitating a by-election in Rejinagar. The Nandigram by-election was necessitated after West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari vacated Nandigram to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated former chief minister Mamata Banerjee in the 2026 Assembly elections. Adhikari had won both constituencies. The contest was closely watched as an early electoral test for the BJP government, which ended the Trinamool Congress’s 15-year rule in West Bengal earlier this year. Hasirani Rath’s candidature draws attention Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, a close aide of Adhikari who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the results of the West Bengal Assembly elections were declared. The BJP backed Rath in the bypoll as the constituency returned to the polls following Adhikari’s decision to retain Bhabanipur. Congress gets TMC support after candidate withdraws The contest also witnessed political realignments within the opposition. The candidate fielded by the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress faction, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the race after meeting Adhikari. Banerjee subsequently extended support to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan. Pradhan’s campaign was also disrupted by his arrest in September in connection with cases dating back to the 2007 Nandigram agitation. He later secured bail from the Calcutta High Court and returned to the constituency to campaign. The Congress had alleged irregularities and intimidation during polling and demanded a repoll. news.headline: MP deputy CM Jagdish Devda’s OSD removed after allegations of ₹1 crore liquor bribe
news.story_lead: MP deputy CM Jagdish Devda’s OSD removed after allegations of ₹1 crore liquor bribe Devda, also the state excise minister, ordered Deepam Raichura’s removal on Friday, and added in a statement that Raichura wasn’t his OSD when he allegedly accepted the bribe. An officer posted on special duty at the Madhya Pradesh deputy chief minister Jagdish Devda’s office was removed from his post after allegations emerged that he had accepted ₹ 1 crore as bribe from a liquor contractor in 2024-25. The allegations against Raichura are contained in a purported statement given to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) by Mohit Gogia, an accused in an alleged ₹ 930 crore fraud linked to nightclubs, restaurants and luxury real estate in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab.
news.full_article_text: MP deputy CM Jagdish Devda’s OSD removed after allegations of ₹1 crore liquor bribe Devda, also the state excise minister, ordered Deepam Raichura’s removal on Friday, and added in a statement that Raichura wasn’t his OSD when he allegedly accepted the bribe. An officer posted on special duty at the Madhya Pradesh deputy chief minister Jagdish Devda’s office was removed from his post after allegations emerged that he had accepted ₹ 1 crore as bribe from a liquor contractor in 2024-25. The allegations against Raichura are contained in a purported statement given to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) by Mohit Gogia, an accused in an alleged ₹ 930 crore fraud linked to nightclubs, restaurants and luxury real estate in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab. A copy of the purported statement went viral on social media recently. HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the social media post. Gogia, a Bhopal resident since 2023, was arrested by the Delhi police in November 2025. In a statement on Friday, Devda said the matter came to his notice through the media and he ordered an inquiry. “During this period, Raichura was posted as assistant excise officer in Bhopal. At that time he was not working as my OSD,” Devda said, adding: “To ensure a fair and impartial probe, Raichura has been immediately relieved from the charge of OSD”. According to the viral copy, Gogia alleged that a person identified as Tanuja Sethi introduced him to Raichura when Raichura was assistant excise commissioner in the excise department. Raichura, in turn, allegedly introduced him to Deepak Dubey, saying Dubey would handle his work. Gogia purportedly claimed in the letter that Raichura helped secure two liquor vends in TT Nagar for 2024-25 in the name of one Jaswant Kumar for ₹ 1 crore. “Of this, ₹ 50 lakh was allegedly paid in cash at a flat in Shalimar Fort Leza on Hoshangabad Road and collected by Deepak Dubey, while the remaining ₹ 50 lakh was allegedly transferred to the bank account of a hotel near ISBT that purportedly belongs to a friend of Raichura,” reads the letter. The purported statement further alleges that a fake fixed deposit receipt (FDR), required as bank guarantee for the liquor contract, was approved with Raichura’s help, and that unlicensed liquor was supplied at the two shops. The statement also includes a mobile number through which Gogia was allegedly in touch with Raichura over calls and chats. Gogia is currently lodged in a jail in connection with the alleged ₹ 930 crore fraud involving around 200 people. The Income Tax Department and the Enforcement Directorate have raided his premises and his assets have been frozen. The viral statement also names several Bhopal-based businessmen with alleged links to senior bureaucrats and politicians. Reacting to this Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari said, “A high level inquiry should be conducted into the matter as it was a serious matter of corruption.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shruti Tomar I have spent over a decade chronicling Madhya Pradesh’s political and social landscape, covering politics, investigative journalism, crime, human interest, and government policy, blending sharp insight with ground‑level depth. I have closely tracked three assembly elections, three Lok Sabha elections, leadership transitions in MP while exposing governance lapses, tender irregularities, and flawed policy rollouts. My reports have revealed gaps in the Cheetah project, irregularities in medical education, rigging in recruitment exams, and loopholes in policy implementation. In crime reporting, I have moved beyond FIRs to map systemic patterns — from organised crime networks and gender‑based violence to custodial accountability — balancing urgency with sensitivity. My journalism is defined by a commitment to human interest. I have profiled the marginalised Bancchda community, documented atrocities against tribal groups, and highlighted efforts to preserve their culture through heritage liquor and revival of spiritual practices. I have reported on farmers struggling with failed MSP promises, giving voice to those often reduced to statistics in policy files. Passionate about field reporting, I have reported on rampant sand mining in Chambal and Narmada, pharmaceutical companies supplying medicines under altered names, the dire condition of schools and colleges, the plight of commercial sex workers, and skewed sex ratios in specific districts. Beyond deadlines, and as HT’s state correspondent and assistant editor in Madhya Pradesh, I engage with ministers, farmers, students, and activists, believing the best policy stories begin with a single human voice. news.full_article_text: 'Don't use hammer to kill a fly': Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi Police to lift blanket curbs on metro, trains The DMRC has announced the closure of 57 metro stations from 9 pm on Friday ahead of the CJP's October 10 protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The Supreme Court on Friday directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of Saturday’s proposed protests in Delhi, making it clear that security measures cannot amount to a complete prohibition on public transport and inconvenience millions of ordinary residents. A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said that authorities could regulate the movement of trains to prevent unlawful gatherings but could not bring the entire system to a halt, stressing that the right of Delhi’s residents to access public facilities and move freely also required protection. “Stopping something and regulating are two different concepts. One can regulate but it is completely different to put a halt on everything…you cannot stop everything,” observed the bench. news.full_article_text: 'Identify other place for protests': Supreme Court calls for alternative to Jantar Mantar in Delhi The Supreme Court on Friday called for a rethink of Delhi’s decades-old arrangement of holding demonstrations at Jantar Mantar The Supreme Court on Friday called for a rethink of Delhi’s decades-old arrangement of holding demonstrations at Jantar Mantar , recording that the Delhi Police commissioner and other competent authorities would consider designating an alternative venue with better facilities for peaceful protesters. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the national capital needed a larger, better-equipped space where citizens could exercise their democratic right to protest without compromising public safety, access to emergency services or the interests of other residents. Also Read | 'Don't use hammer to kill a fly': Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi Police to lift blanket curbs on metro, trains “It is high time that some other place with amenities for peaceful protestors need to be identified and designated,” the bench recorded in its order, adding that the competent authority should consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision. Deep Dive The court also stressed that any alternative site should have basic amenities, including portable cabins, toilets, drinking water and medical facilities. It said a venue must be spacious enough to accommodate demonstrators while allowing emergency services to reach them in the event of an incident. Also Read | 'Please appreciate, see students' future': Top court refuses to reopen FIRs over CJP's July stir The suggestion emerged during the hearing of pleas challenging sweeping restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of the October 10 protests in Delhi. The court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to reconsider the complete stoppage of public transport, emphasising that preventive security measures must remain proportionate and cannot deprive millions of residents of access to essential services. During the hearing, the bench said many of the difficulties surrounding protests arose from Jantar Mantar’s geographical location and suggested that another open space could allow demonstrations to take place with better facilities and fewer logistical complications. “Why don’t you find an alternative space where you can also provide better facilities?” the bench asked solicitor general Tushar Mehta, who appeared for the Centre and Delhi Police. Mehta said he would convey the court’s sentiments to the appropriate authorities. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary Mariam Alexander Baby, responded that Ramlila Maidan had previously served as an alternative protest venue but was no longer being offered as an option when permission to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar was denied. The bench subsequently recorded the parties’ agreement on the need to identify another site. The intervention carries significance because Jantar Mantar has served as Delhi’s principal protest hub for more than three decades, hosting demonstrations by political parties, farmers, trade unions, students and civil society groups. Its location in central Delhi, within reach of Parliament and government offices, has made it a prominent venue for citizens seeking to draw attention to their grievances. The site emerged as the capital’s principal space for organised demonstrations in 1993, after authorities moved away from the Boat Club area near India Gate, where large protests had raised concerns about access to the seat of government and traffic management. In 2017, the National Green Tribunal ordered a ban on protests along Jantar Mantar Road and directed that demonstrators be shifted to Ramlila Maidan, citing complaints about noise, sanitation and the occupation of public space. The Supreme Court set aside the blanket prohibition in July 2018, holding that peaceful demonstrations could not be prohibited altogether, although they could be regulated to protect residents’ rights and maintain public order. The Supreme Court’s latest observations revive the question of whether the existing arrangement adequately balances the right to protest with the practical demands of managing large gatherings in the national capital. The immediate dispute arose after Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar while imposing extensive security measures, including restrictions on metro services and railway movements. The protest, called by the Cockroach Janata Party and other groups, seeks the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral-roll revisions. The bench clarified during the transport hearing that it was not examining the merits of the protest or the organisers’ claims, as the organisers were not before it. Its focus was on safeguarding public access to transport and ensuring that security restrictions did not become a blanket prohibition. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. Beyond daily reportage, Utkarsh has led investigative projects and enterprise reporting that have shaped public debate and prompted institutional responses. His work has received several journalism awards, including the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award. As National Legal Editor, he has also played a key role in expanding Hindustan Times' legal journalism footprint, mentoring reporters and strengthening coverage across platforms. A Chevening South Asia Journalism Programme Fellow, Utkarsh regularly writes analyses on the judiciary and constitutional issues, and his reporting is widely followed by lawyers, judges, policymakers, academics and readers seeking clarity on India's evolving legal landscape. The immediate dispute arose after Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar while imposing extensive security measures, including restrictions on metro services and railway movements. The protest, called by the Cockroach Janata Party and other groups, seeks the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral-roll revisions. The bench clarified during the transport hearing that it was not examining the merits of the protest or the organisers’ claims, as the organisers were not before it. Its focus was on safeguarding public access to transport and ensuring that security restrictions did not become a blanket prohibition. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. Beyond daily reportage, Utkarsh has led investigative projects and enterprise reporting that have shaped public debate and prompted institutional responses. His work has received several journalism awards, including the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award. As National Legal Editor, he has also played a key role in expanding Hindustan Times' legal journalism footprint, mentoring reporters and strengthening coverage across platforms. A Chevening South Asia Journalism Programme Fellow, Utkarsh regularly writes analyses on the judiciary and constitutional issues, and his reporting is widely followed by lawyers, judges, policymakers, academics and readers seeking clarity on India's evolving legal landscape. The Supreme Court on Friday called for a rethink of Delhi’s decades-old arrangement of holding demonstrations at Jantar Mantar

The Supreme Court on Friday called for a rethink of Delhi’s decades-old arrangement of holding demonstrations at Jantar Mantar , recording that the Delhi Police commissioner and other competent authorities would consider designating an alternative venue with better facilities for peaceful protesters.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the national capital needed a larger, better-equipped space where citizens could exercise their democratic right to protest without compromising public safety, access to emergency services or the interests of other residents.

“It is high time that some other place with amenities for peaceful protestors need to be identified and designated,” the bench recorded in its order, adding that the competent authority should consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision.

The court also stressed that any alternative site should have basic amenities, including portable cabins, toilets, drinking water and medical facilities. It said a venue must be spacious enough to accommodate demonstrators while allowing emergency services to reach them in the event of an incident.

news.full_article_text: Over 35,000 property deals worth ₹55,000 crore face Income Tax scrutiny in Gurugram's Badshahpur The exercise may have implications for Gurugram, where high-value property deals are drawing tax authorities’ scrutiny of registrations and financial reporting A survey by the Directorate of Intelligence and Criminal Investigation (I&CI) of the Income Tax Department has detected major deficiencies in the reporting of high-value property transactions at Badshahpur tehsil in Gurugram, with more than 35,000 transactions worth over ₹ 55,000 crore either not reported or incorrectly reported to the department. The survey was conducted at the offices of the state land revenue authorities as part of the Income Tax department’s ongoing exercise to check compliance in reporting high-value immovable property transactions by Tehsildars and Naib Tehsildars. Officials said the transactions flagged during the exercise included cases where details were not furnished to the Income Tax department as well as instances where incorrect Permanent Account Numbers (PANs) had been reported. The department has clarified that the ₹ 55,000 crore figure represents the aggregate value of transactions affected by reporting deficiencies and does not, by itself, represent suspected tax evasion. Their tax implications will be examined separately after verification. Also Read: Haryana rolls out tech-driven land record reforms; auto-mutation to benefit property owners During the survey, officials compared records maintained in the state’s property registration system with Statements of Financial Transactions (SFTs) submitted to the Income Tax department. The exercise revealed substantial gaps between the two sets of records, including omissions and incorrect PAN particulars. Such discrepancies can make it difficult for the tax authorities to identify buyers and sellers and match property transactions with their income-tax records. Officials will now examine whether incorrect PANs were merely reporting errors or were deliberately quoted to conceal the identities of parties involved in the transactions. The Badshahpur findings are part of a wider scrutiny of property registration records in Haryana. The I&CI directorate has conducted several similar surveys over the past year and subsequently apprised senior Haryana revenue authorities of deficiencies in the reporting of property transactions. The Income Tax department has flagged that Tehsildars in several cases either failed to report transactions or furnished incorrect PAN details. The Principal Director General of Income Tax (I&CI), New Delhi, also wrote to the Haryana chief secretary highlighting the deficiencies and the need for corrective action. The state had earlier assured the department that a centralised system for filing SFTs across Haryana would be implemented for 2025-26, with filings to be completed by May 31, 2026. The Inspector General, Revenue, had also assured the department of improved compliance. However, according to the Income Tax department , the filing has deteriorated compared with the previous year. Only around 45 of Haryana’s approximately 140 Tehsildars had filed their SFTs by the time of the latest review, despite the mandatory May 31 deadline. In comparison, more than 120 Tehsildars had filed their SFTs within the prescribed period in the previous year. The department said nearly two-thirds of the Tehsildars had therefore yet to file their SFTs, despite the expiry of the deadline and repeated communication with senior state authorities. Haryana property deals: Reporting mechanism for high-value transactions under scrutiny The findings have put the spotlight on the reporting mechanism for high-value property transactions in Haryana, particularly the accuracy of PAN details and timely filing of SFTs. Accurate reporting is critical for enabling the Income Tax department to link property purchases and sales with the tax records of the individuals and entities involved. The I&CI directorate is expected to continue verifying the transactions identified during the Badshahpur survey and follow up on pending and inaccurate filings. The department has also called for corrective measures by the state to ensure that all pending SFTs are filed and incorrect particulars are rectified. The exercise could have wider implications for Gurugram, where rapid real estate development and high-value property transactions have made the district an important focus of tax authorities’ scrutiny of property registration and financial reporting. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Leena Dhankhar Leena Dhankhar is Senior Editor and Bureau Chief, Gurugram, at Hindustan Times, where she has spent over 17 years chronicling the transformation of one of India's fastest-growing urban regions. From starting her career as a crime reporter to leading the Gurugram bureau, her journalism has been defined by investigative reporting, in-depth storytelling and an unwavering focus on public interest. Over nearly two decades, she has reported extensively across crime, politics, civic governance, elections, real estate, environment, courts, sports, education and entertainment, covering Gurugram, Faridabad, Nuh and Palwal. Her reporting has exposed several major scams and systemic failures, including insurance frauds, waste management irregularities, illegal arms manufacturing units in Nuh, illegal mining in the Aravallis, organised crime networks and governance lapses affecting millions of residents. Known for her investigative work and exclusive stories, Leena has reported on high-impact national issues, including the Nicaragua charter flight carrying Indian migrants that was turned back amid allegations of human trafficking, exposing the growing network of illegal immigration rackets. Her work has also focused on gang wars, prison administration, juvenile crime, women and child protection systems, the functioning of the Juvenile Justice Board and Child Welfare Committee, and environmental challenges such as pollution, waterlogging and deteriorating civic infrastructure. Beyond hard news, Leena has extensively documented Haryana's rich heritage, forests and wildlife, bringing attention to the state's historical landmarks, biodiversity, conservation efforts and ecological challenges through immersive reportage and feature writing. Her journalism has consistently gone beyond breaking news. She has documented Gurugram's rapid urbanisation through long-form narratives and enterprise reporting on issues ranging from pothole-ridden roads, flooding and waste management to the changing social fabric of India's Millennium City. She also writes widely read feature columns, including The Outsider, Changemaker, and Concern for Gurugram, profiling people, places and ideas shaping the city's identity. Leena is the author of Gurugram School Murder, published by Juggernaut Books, a deeply reported account of one of India's most high-profile school murder investigations. Officials said the transactions flagged during the exercise included cases where details were not furnished to the Income Tax department as well as instances where incorrect Permanent Account Numbers (PANs) had been reported. The department has clarified that the ₹ 55,000 crore figure represents the aggregate value of transactions affected by reporting deficiencies and does not, by itself, represent suspected tax evasion. Their tax implications will be examined separately after verification. Also Read: Haryana rolls out tech-driven land record reforms; auto-mutation to benefit property owners During the survey, officials compared records maintained in the state’s property registration system with Statements of Financial Transactions (SFTs) submitted to the Income Tax department. The exercise revealed substantial gaps between the two sets of records, including omissions and incorrect PAN particulars. Such discrepancies can make it difficult for the tax authorities to identify buyers and sellers and match property transactions with their income-tax records. Officials will now examine whether incorrect PANs were merely reporting errors or were deliberately quoted to conceal the identities of parties involved in the transactions. The Badshahpur findings are part of a wider scrutiny of property registration records in Haryana. The I&CI directorate has conducted several similar surveys over the past year and subsequently apprised senior Haryana revenue authorities of deficiencies in the reporting of property transactions. The Income Tax department has flagged that Tehsildars in several cases either failed to report transactions or furnished incorrect PAN details. The Principal Director General of Income Tax (I&CI), New Delhi, also wrote to the Haryana chief secretary highlighting the deficiencies and the need for corrective action. The state had earlier assured the department that a centralised system for filing SFTs across Haryana would be implemented for 2025-26, with filings to be completed by May 31, 2026. The Inspector General, Revenue, had also assured the department of improved compliance. However, according to the Income Tax department , the filing has deteriorated compared with the previous year. Only around 45 of Haryana’s approximately 140 Tehsildars had filed their SFTs by the time of the latest review, despite the mandatory May 31 deadline. In comparison, more than 120 Tehsildars had filed their SFTs within the prescribed period in the previous year. The department said nearly two-thirds of the Tehsildars had therefore yet to file their SFTs, despite the expiry of the deadline and repeated communication with senior state authorities. Haryana property deals: Reporting mechanism for high-value transactions under scrutiny The findings have put the spotlight on the reporting mechanism for high-value property transactions in Haryana, particularly the accuracy of PAN details and timely filing of SFTs. Accurate reporting is critical for enabling the Income Tax department to link property purchases and sales with the tax records of the individuals and entities involved. The I&CI directorate is expected to continue verifying the transactions identified during the Badshahpur survey and follow up on pending and inaccurate filings. The department has also called for corrective measures by the state to ensure that all pending SFTs are filed and incorrect particulars are rectified. The exercise could have wider implications for Gurugram, where rapid real estate development and high-value property transactions have made the district an important focus of tax authorities’ scrutiny of property registration and financial reporting. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Leena Dhankhar Leena Dhankhar is Senior Editor and Bureau Chief, Gurugram, at Hindustan Times, where she has spent over 17 years chronicling the transformation of one of India's fastest-growing urban regions. Her work has also focused on gang wars, prison administration, juvenile crime, women and child protection systems, the functioning of the Juvenile Justice Board and Child Welfare Committee, and environmental challenges such as pollution, waterlogging and deteriorating civic infrastructure. Beyond hard news, Leena has extensively documented Haryana's rich heritage, forests and wildlife, bringing attention to the state's historical landmarks, biodiversity, conservation efforts and ecological challenges through immersive reportage and feature writing. Her journalism has consistently gone beyond breaking news. news.story_lead: Nandigram bypoll result: BJP's Hasirani Rath leads in early trends for key West Bengal seat As ECI counts the votes for the Nandigram bypolls, heavy security has been deployed at the counting centres. The counting of votes for the Nandigram by-elections is underway by the Election Commission of India. As per early trends from ECI, Hasirani Rath, the candidate fielded by the BJP, is in the lead.
news.full_article_text: Nandigram bypoll result: BJP's Hasirani Rath leads in early trends for key West Bengal seat As ECI counts the votes for the Nandigram bypolls, heavy security has been deployed at the counting centres. The counting of votes for the Nandigram by-elections is underway by the Election Commission of India. As per early trends from ECI, Hasirani Rath, the candidate fielded by the BJP, is in the lead. Nandigram, which is in West Bengal's East Midnapore, went to the polls on October 6 and saw a turnout of 80.89 per cent. The seat fell vacant after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who won from both Nandigram and Bhabanipur, retained the latter. Track LIVE updates on bypoll election results As per data from the Election Commission, BJP's Hasirani Rath is in the lead with a total of 11,965 votes. Based on this number, the BJP candidate is ahead by a margin of over 9,500 votes from Congress's Milan Pradhan. High security in Nandigram The Nandigram bypoll is among the first electoral battles in West Bengal after the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in May this year with a sweeping victory, ousting the 15-year-old Mamata Banerjee regime, and the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) split into two factions. West Bengal witnessed high political drama in the run-up to the by-polls in which Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the candidate fielded by Mamata Banerjee in Nandigram, withdrew her nomination hours after meeting West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. Soon after Dey resigned, Banerjee announced that the Mamata-AITC led by her would support Milan Pradhan, the Congress candidate in Nandigram. Hours later, Pradhan was arrested by the police in the 2007 murder cases, but was granted bail by the Calcutta high court. news.headline: Class 10 boy found dead inside classmate's house in Faridabad, cops injured as families clash
news.story_lead: Class 10 boy found dead inside classmate's house in Faridabad, cops injured as families clash Police said the boy and his female classmate, both minors, were studying in standard 10 at a private school in Faridabad. A class 10 boy was found dead under mysterious circumstances at a classmate's house in Faridabad’s Shiv Shakti enclave on Thursday night, police said on Friday. While the boy’s family alleged that he was murdered, the girl’s family said that he used to stalk her and had sneaked inside their home on Thursday night and hanged himself.
news.full_article_text: Class 10 boy found dead inside classmate's house in Faridabad, cops injured as families clash Police said the boy and his female classmate, both minors, were studying in standard 10 at a private school in Faridabad. A class 10 boy was found dead under mysterious circumstances at a classmate's house in Faridabad’s Shiv Shakti enclave on Thursday night, police said on Friday. While the boy’s family alleged that he was murdered, the girl’s family said that he used to stalk her and had sneaked inside their home on Thursday night and hanged himself. Two cops were injured in a clash that broke out after family members found the boy dead under mysterious circumstances at the girl's house. What we know The victim, 17, was a resident of Sai Nagar Part-II and had travelled to the girl’s residence located in Shiv Shakti enclave. Investigators said that it was the girl’s family which had alerted the police control room that the victim had died by suicide, after which the boy’s family also reached the spot, following which a clash broke out. A senior police officer said that the boy’s family barged into the girl’s house and assaulted her family members, alleging that they had murdered him and hanged the body from the ceiling to make it look like a suicide. “They ransacked the entire house after which police personnel were rushed to the spot in addition to those already present at the spot for investigation to bring the situation under control,” he said, adding the two cops had sustained minor injuries in the clash. Investigators said that the situation was brought under control after an almost an hour-long effort to separate both families. They said the body was taken into custody from the girl’s home and sent to the mortuary at Badshah Khan Civil Hospital, where an autopsy will be carried out on Friday. Yashpal Yadav, public relations officer of Faridabad police, said that the girl’s family has alleged that they had even submitted a complaint in the school against the victim for harassing her. “As per the girl’s family, he had apologised and promised not to follow her again in school. These things will be clear after the school principal, teachers and classmates are quizzed,” he said. Yadav said that it will be clear from the autopsy whether the boy died by suicide or was murdered. “Necessary legal action will be taken accordingly in the case after the post-mortem report is received, in which case the cause of death will become clear,” he added. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debashish Karmakar Debashish Karmakar is a principal correspondent with the Hindustan Times, Gurugram bureau. He has a vast journalistic experience of almost 14 years of covering crime, court, power, transport, administration, weather and other beats while working across various organisations. He has been covering Gurugram, Faridabad, Nuh, Palwal and other districts of southern Haryana for more than four and a half years. He has produced several breaking and exclusive stories while reporting from the ground where he maintains a strong presence on a daily basis. He writes news articles which are hard-hitting and accurate. With his strong bureaucratic sources, he frequently writes stories to expose the failure of the system forcing authorities to take necessary course-corrective steps. Besides crime, important convictions and court orders, he also writes on human-angle stories, on power issues and challenges faced by the residents on a daily basis in Gurugram and neighbouring areas. In the past, he worked for media houses like The Times of India, where he extensively reported on important government matters and daily proceedings at the Patna High Court. He has also worked in the electronic media and had done ground coverage on the Kedarnath deluge that wrecked Uttarakhand in 2013. Read More

news.full_article_text: Mayawati pays tribute to Kanshi Ram on death anniversary Lucknow, BSP president Mayawati on Friday paid tributes to party founder Kanshi Ram on his death anniversary, recalling that the party formed the government four times in Uttar Pradesh under her leadership and asserting that his mission helped advance the cause of social transformation and economic emancipation. In a post on X, Mayawati said Kanshi Ram had worked to empower Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other weaker sections by helping them use their voting power to gain political authority. "To provide the master key of power to crores of Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other weaker sections of the Bahujan Samaj, who have been oppressed and pushed back for centuries on the basis of caste, through the strength of their votes, and to carry forward the stalled and scattered caravan of self-respect and dignity of their messiah, the revered Baba Saheb Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar, towards its destination," she said, paying homage to Kanshi Ram on behalf of the BSP family. She described Kanshi Ram as the founder of the Bahujan Samaj Party and offered her heartfelt tributes to him on his death anniversary. Mayawati said it was the result of his mission-driven resolve that the BSP formed the government four times in Uttar Pradesh under her leadership. "Through these governments, historic work of social transformation and economic emancipation was undertaken, drawing inspiration from social reformers and leaders, including Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, Narayana Guru, Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj and B R Ambedkar," Mayawati said. Their struggles and contributions towards securing rights based on equality, she said, were translated into action at the grassroots level to fulfil the spirit of the Constitution. Mayawati further said the BSP governments had sought to honour Kanshi Ram's legacy by establishing the rule of law through crime control and law and order measures, while also working for public welfare, development and the interests of all sections of society in Uttar Pradesh. She described the party's governance record as a tribute to the ideals and mission of its founder. Kanshi Ram, a social reformer and political leader, was born on March 15, 1934, in Punjab, and passed away on October 9, 2006. He founded the Bahujan Samaj Party in 1984. news.full_article_text: Supreme Court raps Kerala govt for not detailing steps to protect state's tallest captive elephant The court questioned Kerala’s claim that it had taken the elephant's custody after the June 9 order, asking why the fact had not been disclosed in its affidavit The Supreme Court on Friday pulled up the Kerala government for failing to place on record the steps taken to safeguard Uttoly Raman -- the state’s tallest captive elephant, since it ordered the animal’s custody to be transferred to the state in June, directing authorities to produce his latest medical examination report on October 12. A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu questioned the state’s claim that it had taken custody of the elephant soon after the June 9 order, asking why the fact had not been disclosed in its affidavit and why the court had been kept in the dark about the steps taken to ensure the animal’s welfare. “What were you doing since June 9? What happened since June? Where is that recorded in your affidavit?” the bench asked the state’s counsel, who cited the assembly elections in Kerala as one of the reasons for the delay. “It is a wonderful argument to make. So, the Supreme Court order is not to be complied with all these months because there were elections?” retorted the court, expressing displeasure over what it described as an attempt to avoid compliance with its directions. “This is just a ploy. The state does not want to comply,” the bench said, questioning why Raman had been allowed to remain in the custody of his caretaker, Krishnankutty, despite the court’s direction to transfer him to the state. When the state’s counsel said the elephant was already in government custody, the bench asked when the transfer had taken place and why the fact had not been mentioned in the affidavit. The court also directed the state to ensure that Krishnankutty was not allowed to touch the elephant. “The only love and affection you have for the elephant is for the love of money. You have commercially exploited the elephant,” the bench told the caretaker, who was found guilty of contempt in June for violating an undertaking that Raman would not be used for commercial or temple activities. The state informed the court that it had a medical report from June. Questioning whether the elephant had undergone any medical examination since then, the bench directed the government to produce the latest report at the next hearing. “The state shall duly comply with the court’s June 9 order in letter and spirit and will take proper care of the elephant,” directed the court, asking the authorities to place the latest medical inspection report on record by October 12. The proceedings arise from a protracted dispute over Raman’s ownership between the Mata Amritanandamayi Mutt, which claims that the elephant was entrusted to Krishnankutty only for care and maintenance, and the latter, who claims ownership on the basis of two gift deeds executed in February 2017. On June 9, the Supreme Court, while dealing with the dispute, ordered the Kerala government to take over the elephant’s custody and ensure his welfare, holding that the caretaker had violated a solemn undertaking given to the court on August 6, 2025, that the animal would not be used for religious or commercial activities. The breach came to light through a state inspection report submitted to the court, which recorded that Raman had been taken to a temple festival near Chavakkad. Krishnankutty subsequently apologised, citing religious considerations and the illness of another elephant that was scheduled to participate in the ceremony. Rejecting the explanation, the bench had held at the time that the court could not turn a blind eye to the exploitation of an animal that could not speak for itself. It found Krishnankutty guilty of contempt and imposed a fine of ₹ 2,000, while directing the state to take over Raman’s custody and place him in an appropriate rescue or rehabilitation facility. The custody arrangement is an interim measure pending a final decision in the underlying criminal appeals. The Mutt has alleged that the gift deeds relied upon by Krishnankutty were fabricated and that the purported transfer was contrary to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which places Asian elephants under the highest level of statutory protection and regulates their transfer and possession. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. Beyond daily reportage, Utkarsh has led investigative projects and enterprise reporting that have shaped public debate and prompted institutional responses. His work has received several journalism awards, including the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award. As National Legal Editor, he has also played a key role in expanding Hindustan Times' legal journalism footprint, mentoring reporters and strengthening coverage across platforms. bullet_points: Supreme Court raps Kerala govt for not detailing steps to protect state's tallest captive elephant
The court questioned Kerala’s claim that it had taken the elephant's custody after the June 9 order, asking why the fact had not been disclosed in its affidavit

The Supreme Court on Friday pulled up the Kerala government for failing to place on record the steps taken to safeguard Uttoly Raman -- the state’s tallest captive elephant, since it ordered the animal’s custody to be transferred to the state in June, directing authorities to produce his latest medical examination report on October 12.

A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu questioned the state’s claim that it had taken custody of the elephant soon after the June 9 order, asking why the fact had not been disclosed in its affidavit and why the court had been kept in the dark about the steps taken to ensure the animal’s welfare.

“What were you doing since June 9? What happened since June? Where is that recorded in your affidavit?” the bench asked the state’s counsel, who cited the assembly elections in Kerala as one of the reasons for the delay.

“It is a wonderful argument to make. So, the Supreme Court order is not to be complied with all these months because there were elections?” retorted the court, expressing displeasure over what it described as an attempt to avoid compliance with its directions.

“This is just a ploy. The state does not want to comply,” the bench said, questioning why Raman had been allowed to remain in the custody of his caretaker, Krishnankutty, despite the court’s direction to transfer him to the state.

When the state’s counsel said the elephant was already in government custody, the bench asked when the transfer had taken place and why the fact had not been mentioned in the affidavit. The court also directed the state to ensure that Krishnankutty was not allowed to touch the elephant.

news.headline: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
news.story_lead: Watch: Houses underwater and families trapped by floodwaters in Chile - Published 8 October 2026 Police in central Chile have airlifted several residents to safety after rising floodwaters left them trapped in their homes. Recent torrential rains caused the Mapocho river to burst its banks, flooding large parts of the city of Talagante, 35km (22 miles) south-west of the capital, Santiago. Santiago has seen 74mm of rainfall in the first seven days of this month, making it the rainiest October for the area in 76 years, meteorologists have said.

news.exam_corner_topic: Mamata Banerjee may join CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10
news.headline: Mamata Banerjee may join CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10
news.story_lead: Mamata Banerjee may join CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 Mamata Banerjee said she may join the CJP’s October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Thursday said she may join the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as the INDIA bloc prepares to march to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday. Banerjee reached the residence of her nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in Kolkata.
news.full_article_text: Mamata Banerjee may join CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 Mamata Banerjee said she may join the CJP’s October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Thursday said she may join the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as the INDIA bloc prepares to march to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday. Banerjee reached the residence of her nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in Kolkata. She is also expected to be part of a 10-member core team of INDIA bloc leaders that will meet President Droupadi Murmu on Friday to submit a memorandum against alleged mass disenfranchisement and demand Kumar’s ouster. “I may join the protest at Jantar Mantar scheduled for October 10, but nothing can be confirmed now. We have maintained a relationship with them (the CJP) and have extended our support, while any further decision regarding our participation will be taken later,” Banerjee said in Kolkata. Deep Dive Banerjee had played a key role in expediting the protest plans at the INDIA bloc meeting on September 29 and had earned Congress Parliamentary Party chief Sonia Gandhi’s support. She returned here as the CJP is set to start a dharna amid the INDIA bloc’s prolonged protests. When asked if she would join the CJP’s dharna at Jantar Mantar, Trinamool’s Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien said, “As you all know we support the CJP. We have good relationship with some of their leaders. We know Abhijeet Dipke for years. Ashutosh Ranka came to Kolkata and we had lunch. I am neither confirming nor denying if Mamata Banerjee will participate in the CJP protests.” While the Congress remains suspicious of the CJP and dubs it as an ally of Arvind Kejriwal’s Aam Aadmi Party, Trinamool and Shiv Sena (UBT) have extended olive branches to the new outfit. During the CJP’s protests against the exam paper leak, Banerjee sent five MPs to the CJP’s platform to express solidarity. “I was asked to go, so I am going... A request for an appointment with the President has been made for the 8th or 9th on behalf of the INDIA Alliance leaders; my name has been included in that list,” Banerjee said. INDIA bloc lawmakers will march from Parliament to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday to meet President Droupadi over the raging issue of mass disenfranchisement through SIR. They will also demand Kumar’s ouster. The Rashtrapati Bhavan, however, has not yet finalised the Opposition’s appointment to meet Murmu, who was in Himachal Pradesh for the past three days.

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Thursday said she may join the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as the INDIA bloc prepares to march to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday.

Banerjee reached the residence of her nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in Kolkata. She is also expected to be part of a 10-member core team of INDIA bloc leaders that will meet President Droupadi Murmu on Friday to submit a memorandum against alleged mass disenfranchisement and demand Kumar’s ouster.

“I may join the protest at Jantar Mantar scheduled for October 10, but nothing can be confirmed now. We have maintained a relationship with them (the CJP) and have extended our support, while any further decision regarding our participation will be taken later,” Banerjee said in Kolkata.

Banerjee had played a key role in expediting the protest plans at the INDIA bloc meeting on September 29 and had earned Congress Parliamentary Party chief Sonia Gandhi’s support. She returned here as the CJP is set to start a dharna amid the INDIA bloc’s prolonged protests.

news.headline: Four CRPF personnel injured in accidental blast while disposing explosives in Chhattisgarh
news.story_lead: Four CRPF personnel injured in accidental blast while disposing explosives in Chhattisgarh Four CRPF personnel, including two ASIs, were injured in an accidental blast while disposing of unserviceable and leftover explosives near a camp in Sukma. Four Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel, including two assistant sub-inspectors (ASI), were injured in an accidental blast while a team was disposing of unserviceable and leftover explosives near a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh’s Sukma district on Thursday, police said. The incident took place near Bodrajpadar Nala, around 200 metres from the Elarmadgu camp.
news.full_article_text: Four CRPF personnel injured in accidental blast while disposing explosives in Chhattisgarh Four CRPF personnel, including two ASIs, were injured in an accidental blast while disposing of unserviceable and leftover explosives near a camp in Sukma. Four Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel, including two assistant sub-inspectors (ASI), were injured in an accidental blast while a team was disposing of unserviceable and leftover explosives near a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh’s Sukma district on Thursday, police said. The incident took place near Bodrajpadar Nala, around 200 metres from the Elarmadgu camp. According to a police statement, an Ammunition Technician Team (ATT) from Jagdalpur had reached the 50th Battalion CRPF’s Elarmadgu camp to inspect various camps in the Konta range and safely dispose of unserviceable and remaining explosives stored there. During the disposal process, which was being carried out following safety protocols, a piece of an explosive or bomb accidentally flew towards the nearby area and exploded, injuring four personnel. Those injured were identified as ASI M K Tiwari of the ATT team, ASI Aneesh Khan of the 50th Battalion CRPF, Inspector Amarnath Mishra of the ATT team and head constable Kuldeep Raj of the 50th Battalion CRPF. Tiwari and Khan suffered serious injuries, while Mishra and Raj sustained minor injuries, the statement added. All four were given first aid immediately after the incident and shifted to the government hospital in Konta, where treatment was underway. The seriously injured personnel were being prepared for referral to a higher medical facility, if required, police said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ritesh Mishra Ritesh Mishra is the State Correspondent for Chhattisgarh with Hindustan Times. He reports on Maoism, internal security, politics, mining, governance, and major developments shaping the state. Based in Raipur, he has covered Chhattisgarh since 2016, reporting extensively from the Bastar region and other conflict-affected areas. With nearly two decades of experience in journalism, Ritesh has built a reputation for ground reporting from some of India's most challenging terrains. His coverage spans Left-Wing Extremism, counter-insurgency operations, elections, tribal affairs, environmental issues, infrastructure, mining, and socio-economic developments. He has reported on major security operations, policy initiatives, wildlife crime, and the changing dynamics of conflict and development in Central India. Before moving to Chhattisgarh, Ritesh spent eight years reporting from Madhya Pradesh, covering politics, administration, crime, development, and social issues. Throughout his career, he has reported on various forms of extremism in Central India, combining field reporting with in-depth analysis to produce accurate, balanced, and impactful journalism. Prior to joining Hindustan Times, Ritesh worked with The Pioneer and The Free Press Journal, where he covered a wide range of beats and honed his skills in political, investigative, and field reporting. His reporting is marked by exclusive stories, extensive fieldwork, and a commitment to factual, on-the-ground journalism that brings complex issues to a wider audience. Read More

news.full_article_text: CAPF Act notified two days before SC special bench hearing pleas against it The Centre on Thursday notified the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, bringing it into force from October 8 The Centre on Thursday notified the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, bringing it into force from October 8, a week before a Supreme Court special bench is scheduled to hear petitions challenging the law filed by serving CAPF cadre officers. On October 15, the special bench is scheduled to hear two petitions — one filed last year over the Centre’s alleged failure to implement the Supreme Court’s May 2025 order on cadre review, promotions and deputation of IPS officers to the CAPFs, and another filed this year challenging the new law. The officers, who won the case in May 2025 after a decade-long legal battle, have argued that the law seeks to circumvent the apex court’s order and continues the structural disadvantage faced by cadre officers. The Act governs the functioning and administration of all Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs). A gazette notification issued by the Union home ministry said, “In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (2) of section 1 of the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026 (9 of 2026), the Central Government hereby appoints the 08th day of October, 2026, as the date on which the provisions of the said Act shall come into force.” Serving cadre officers, including recipients of Shaurya Chakra and other gallantry awards, have challenged the law in the Supreme Court, arguing that it is discriminatory, was enacted to override the court’s judgment and that the directions issued last year were never implemented by the home ministry. While the Supreme Court had directed the government to progressively reduce the deputation of IPS officers, the new law fixes the number of posts for IPS and cadre officers at different ranks. The petitioners have argued that this would hurt the career prospects of cadre officers by limiting their chances of reaching senior leadership positions. For instance, the Act provides that the posts of director general (DG) and special DG will be filled only by IPS officers. The Centre introduced the CAPF General Administration Bill, 2026, in the Rajya Sabha on March 27. The bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha on April 1 and the Lok Sabha on April 2, amid protests by opposition leaders who said it would affect the morale of cadre officers. The law comes nearly a year after the Supreme Court ruled in favour of CAPF cadre officers following a decade-long legal battle over cadre review, timely promotions and leadership roles, including reducing the deputation of IPS officers to the forces. The officers had told the top court that despite being members of Group A services and serving in senior ranks throughout their careers, they could not rise to leadership positions because IPS officers were brought in from outside on deputation. The Supreme Court ruled in their favour on May 23, 2025, directing the Centre to progressively reduce IPS deputation, among other measures. It also directed a cadre review to enable timely promotions for cadre officers. The Centre’s review petition was dismissed on October 28, 2025. The bill was introduced in March 2026 even though the judgment had not been implemented. While introducing the new law, the home ministry said IPS officers were essential for the effective functioning of the CAPFs and Centre-state coordination. “Under Article 312 of the Constitution, the Indian Police Service is an All India Service, and the officers of the Service are posted in the Union and the States. Historically, IPS officers are an integral and important part of the CAPFs, who have been serving on deputation along with officers and members of these Forces. The CAPFs perform functions relating to national security and anti-insurgency in close coordination with the State authorities. Therefore, in the interest of maintaining Centre-State relations by ensuring close coordination between the Union and the States for effective operational functioning, it is essential to maintain the existing system of deputation of the IPS Officers in the CAPFs,” the statement of objects and reasons in the bill said. While fixing the sanctioned strength of IPS and cadre officers in the CAPFs, the government also said the absence of an umbrella law had led to regulatory provisions evolving in a fragmented manner, resulting in several service-related litigations and functional and administrative difficulties.

The Centre on Thursday notified the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, bringing it into force from October 8, a week before a Supreme Court special bench is scheduled to hear petitions challenging the law filed by serving CAPF cadre officers.

news.headline: Bihar EOU recovers ₹52 lakh cash, ₹35 lakh ornaments from executive engineer’s premises
